old_problem: RAID0 title conflicted with [0|1|5] syntax and Criteria requiring fail/remove/add/rebuild, even though RAID0 has no redundant rebuild; fixed /dev paths and broad zero-superblock were unsafe.
disposition_reason: ED-01 authoritatively states RAID0 must not execute RAID Rebuild. This row is therefore retained as RAID0-only create, filesystem, file-integrity and teardown coverage; the Procedure section explicitly limited to RAID1/5 and its corresponding rebuild Criteria are non-applicable here. Exact devices remain runtime parameters under destructive authorization.

test_case.test_name: Parameterized destructive mdadm RAID0 create, file-integrity and teardown validation
test_case.purpose: Verify an approved disposable four-member NVMe mdadm RAID0 can be created, formatted, mounted, used for the specified 512 MiB file copy/integrity check, unmounted, stopped and precisely cleaned without claiming redundancy or rebuild.
required_package: Four disposable NVMe serial/NGUID-to-stable-device mappings and approved /dev/md path
Critical destructive authorization proving all members are non-boot, unmounted, non-swap, non-LVM, non-RAID and contain no valuable data
Approved mount path, 512 MiB source file/hash method and runtime window
Exact teardown list, OOB access, abort criteria and recovery/disposition
test_case.test_command: After independent stable-identity and exclusion checks plus explicit approval, create only mdadm RAID0 at level=0 with the four approved members, verify all members and array geometry, mkfs.ext4, mount, create/copy the 512 MiB file and compare source/destination hashes, then unmount, stop and zero superblocks only on the same four recorded members. Do not fail, remove, add or rebuild a RAID0 member.
test_case.expected_result: The exact level-0 array and filesystem become healthy/usable, copied file hash matches the source, and teardown removes only the approved array metadata; no rebuild state is expected or accepted.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact member identity, mdadm level=0 state, successful filesystem/mount, matching source and destination hashes, clean unmount/stop and precise metadata cleanup. Any member fault/rebuild claim is invalid for RAID0.
safety_gate: Destructive approval is mandatory before mdadm --create, mkfs or zero-superblock.
Exclude OS/boot/EFI, mounted, swap, LVM/device-mapper, existing RAID, management and valuable-data devices using stable identities.
Use unique explicit members and one approved md path; never reuse a placeholder or broad device glob.
Abort on identity drift, unexpected existing signatures, array/member error, mount outside approved path, I/O/thermal/power error or failed unmount; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Critical authorization and four-member serial/NGUID map
Exact mdadm create/detail and RAID0 geometry
mkfs/mount plus source/destination 512 MiB file hashes
Unmount/stop/targeted zero-superblock outputs, final lsblk/md state and system logs
test_case.recovery: On any mismatch, stop before the next destructive phase, preserve mdadm/member/signature/mount/log evidence, do not zero metadata or assemble with guesses, and require the storage owner to choose recovery. Teardown proceeds only when the mounted filesystem is cleanly unmounted and all member identities still match.
